entries.name: Deposition (geology)
entries.definition: The geological process by which sediment, soil or rock is laid down on a landform or land mass.

entries.name: Design consultation
entries.definition: Advising clients on design choices, such as the look, layout or function of a space, product or service.

entries.name: Design documentation
entries.definition: Writing and maintaining the drawings, specifications and notes that record how something is designed.

entries.name: Design for manufacturability
entries.definition: Designing a product so that it is easy and cheap to make, by taking production methods and limits into account from the start.

entries.name: Design of experiments
entries.definition: Planning experiments so that the effects of several factors on a result can be measured efficiently and fairly.

entries.name: Design review
entries.definition: A formal checkpoint where a design is examined against its requirements so that problems are found before work continues.

entries.name: Design validation
entries.definition: Checking, usually by testing, that a finished design meets the needs of its users and its intended use.

entries.name: Desktop management
entries.definition: Setting up, updating, securing and supporting an organisation's desktop computers and their software.

entries.name: Desmos
entries.definition: A free online graphing calculator and set of maths learning tools.

entries.name: Destoner
entries.definition: A farm machine that separates stones and clods from soil, used to prepare fields for root crops such as potatoes.

entries.name: Deterministic methods
entries.definition: Methods whose result is fully determined by their inputs, with no randomness involved.

entries.name: Dethatcher
entries.definition: A machine or hand tool that removes thatch, the layer of dead grass and roots, from a lawn.

entries.name: Developmentally appropriate practice
entries.definition: An approach to early childhood teaching that fits activities to children's age, individual needs and cultural background, as set out by the National Association for the Education of Young Children.

entries.name: DevExpress
entries.definition: A suite of user-interface component and reporting libraries for .NET, web and other application development, sold by the company DevExpress.

entries.name: Deviation investigation
entries.definition: Finding the cause of a departure from an approved procedure or specification, mainly in regulated manufacturing such as pharmaceuticals, and recording the findings.

entries.name: Deviation management
entries.definition: The process of recording, investigating, assessing and closing out departures from approved procedures in regulated manufacturing such as pharmaceuticals.

entries.name: DevOps
entries.definition: Coordinating software delivery and operations workflows.

entries.name: DevSecOps
entries.definition: Building security checks into every stage of software development and delivery as part of a DevOps workflow.

entries.name: Diagnostic analysis
entries.definition: Examining data or a system's behaviour to work out why something happened or went wrong.

entries.name: Diagnostic audiology
entries.definition: The branch of audiology that tests hearing and balance to identify and measure disorders.

entries.name: Dialectology
entries.definition: The study of regional and social varieties of a language.

entries.name: Dialogflow
entries.definition: Google Cloud's platform for building chatbots and voice agents that understand natural language.

entries.name: Dictaphone
entries.definition: A device for recording speech so that it can be played back and typed up later.

entries.name: Dictation
entries.definition: Taking down spoken words as text, or speaking text aloud so that it can be recorded and typed up.

entries.name: Dietetics
entries.definition: The science and practice of using food and nutrition to promote health and treat disease.

entries.name: Digital accessibility
entries.definition: Designing digital experiences usable by people with disabilities.

entries.name: Digital advertising
entries.definition: Planning, buying and running paid advertisements on digital channels such as search, social media and websites.

entries.name: Digital.ai
entries.definition: A software delivery platform from the company Digital.ai that covers agile planning, release and deployment automation, and application security.

entries.name: Digital communications
entries.definition: Communicating with people through digital channels such as email, messaging, video calls and social media.

entries.name: Digital currencies
entries.definition: Money that exists only in electronic form, including cryptocurrencies and central bank digital currencies.

entries.name: Digital customer strategy
entries.definition: Defining how a business will attract, serve and keep customers through digital channels, and the plan for achieving that.

entries.name: Digital fluency
entries.definition: Using digital tools confidently and choosing the right one for the task.

entries.name: Digital health technologies
entries.definition: Technologies used in health care and wellbeing, such as telehealth, electronic health records, wearables and health apps.

entries.name: Digital humanities
entries.definition: A field that applies computing methods, such as text analysis and digital archives, to the study of the humanities.

entries.name: Digital journalism
entries.definition: Gathering and reporting news for online outlets, using digital tools such as social media, multimedia and audience analytics.

entries.name: Digital merchandising
entries.definition: Selecting, arranging and promoting products on a website or app to help shoppers find and buy them.

entries.name: Digital Private Network Signalling System
entries.definition: A signalling protocol, developed by British Telecom, that lets private telephone exchanges of different makers share calls and features over digital links.

entries.name: Digital rights management
entries.definition: Technology and policy for controlling how copyrighted digital content can be accessed, copied and shared.

entries.name: Digital skills
entries.definition: Being able to use computers, software and online services to do everyday and work tasks.

entries.name: Digital transformation
entries.definition: Using digital technology to change how an organisation works, serves its customers and competes.
